content.teaser: We invite submissions addressing grammatical diversity, corpus standardisation, bio-phonetics, and digital equity in South Asian languages.
content.markdown:
### Core Tracks
- **Track 1: Low-Resource Speech & Language Modeling** 
  Methods for training automated models on under-represented phonetics, low-resource syntax, and code-mixed formats.
- **Track 2: Ethical Corpus Collection & Royalties** 
  Legal frameworks, policy, and mechanisms for rewarding minoritised communities for language contributions.
- **Track 3: Digital Heritage & Semantic Archiving** 
  Technological pathways to index, classify, and host historic field recordings under fair semantic access schemas.

### Submission Guidelines
Abstracts should not exceed 2 pages including references. Please format using the standard [CoDIN ACL-Style Paper Template](https://aclweb.org) or refer to the [Author Guidelines & Kit](https://github.com). All submissions must be anonymous for double-blind review. Accepted papers will be indexed in the [South Asian Digital Language Library](https://codin.org.in). For questions regarding track alignment, review our [Call for Papers Portal](https://codin.org.in) or email <summit2026@codin.org.in>.

projects.title: Project Kailash
projects.description: Collecting large-scale training data across minoritised and tribal languages. Our mission is to reduce AI's bias by building fundamental benchmarking and training datasets for excluded cultures.
projects.longDescription: Project Kailash is CDI's ambitious response to the digital language divide. Currently, AI models suffer from profound data bias, often failing to recognize the nuances of minoritised or tribal languages. This project focuses on the large-scale acquisition of high-quality training and benchmarking datasets specifically for these excluded communities. By creating structural parity in the digital landscape, we ensure that the next generation of AI is inclusive from the ground up.
projects.methodology: We employ a hybrid approach combining field linguistics with automated quality-assurance pipelines. Our W2M certified annotators work directly with community native speakers to ensure cultural authenticity and linguistic precision.
impact: Targeting 10+ minoritised languages in phase one.
Developing baseline transformers for low-resource varieties.
Reducing AI bias in speech-to-text accuracy by 40%.

content.teaser: We operate a 'Sovereign Language Data' royalty framework.
content.markdown: Every spoken contribution captured for Project Kailash is cryptographically mapped to the speaker's guild. Direct micro-royalties are governed through community co-ops to prevent algorithmic exploitation or uncompensated digital enclosure of indigenous oral resources. Commercial adapters must pay a local linguist equity premium.

projects.title: Tholkudi
projects.description: A government-supported language and cultural documentation initiative focused on preserving the linguistic, oral, ecological, and cultural heritage of Tamil Nadu’s Scheduled Tribe communities through digital archiving, field documentation, and public access systems. The project contributes to safeguarding intangible cultural heritage through community-centered archival and documentation practices.
projects.longDescription:
Tholkudi is a large-scale language and cultural documentation initiative supported by the Government of Tamil Nadu and developed to document, preserve, and improve long-term access to the linguistic and cultural heritage of Scheduled Tribe communities across Tamil Nadu. The project brings together language documentation, oral traditions, folklore, ecological knowledge, songs, narratives, ritual practices, material culture, and community histories into a structured digital archival environment intended for long-term preservation and public accessibility.

Karthick Narayanan served as consultant for language documentation and played a major role in shaping the archive’s documentation architecture, metadata approach, multilingual archival structure, and broader conceptual direction. His work contributed substantially to the development of the archive’s documentation workflows and approaches to representing linguistic and cultural knowledge within a digital archival system. In continuation of this work, the Council for Diversity and Innovation (CoDIN) was later entrusted with implementing a user-centered redesign and accessibility-oriented archival interface for the repository. This phase focused on improving discoverability, metadata navigation, browsing systems, multilingual accessibility, mobile responsiveness, and overall public usability of archival collections.

The redesign process emphasized practical archival usability for researchers, students, educators, government stakeholders, and community members while maintaining compatibility with long-term digital preservation standards.

The project combines field documentation, digital humanities approaches, metadata-driven archival systems, and participatory methods of cultural preservation. Particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that archival representation remains context-sensitive, community-informed, and publicly accessible.

Rather than functioning solely as a storage repository, Tholkudi is envisioned as a living cultural knowledge platform supporting research, education, cultural continuity, public engagement, and future heritage preservation initiatives related to Tamil Nadu’s indigenous and tribal communities.
projects.methodology:
The project follows a field-based and archival-centered documentation methodology combining ethnographic fieldwork, oral history collection, audiovisual recording, metadata creation, transcription, cataloguing, and digital preservation workflows.

Documentation activities include recording oral traditions, linguistic practices, folklore, ecological knowledge, songs, narratives, and cultural practices from communities across Tamil Nadu. The archival infrastructure integrates multilingual metadata systems, structured browsing frameworks, and user-centered design principles to improve accessibility and discoverability.

The later redesign and implementation phase carried out by the Council for Diversity and Innovation focused on improving archival usability through multilingual interfaces, mobile-responsive design, metadata-driven discovery systems, structured browsing environments, and public-facing archival navigation tools.
impact: Documentation and preservation of linguistic and cultural heritage associated with Scheduled Tribe communities in Tamil Nadu.
Creation of a publicly accessible digital archive for language and cultural materials.
Development of multilingual and metadata-rich archival systems for cultural preservation.
Improved usability and discoverability of archival collections through user-centered interface redesign.
Strengthening long-term digital preservation infrastructure for cultural heritage materials.
Contribution to safeguarding intangible cultural heritage through digital documentation and archival accessibility.
